title: NerveCenter: Cost Optimization Initiative Cadence & Tracking
creator: Asha Menon
description: Create and operate a single initiative tracker (NerveCenter) that coordinates experiments, rollouts, and OKR telemetry for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization across Redwood deployments. The goal is to create predictable, repeatable practice for: (1) hypothesis-driven experiments that measure token-per-dollar improvements, (2) safety guardrails for quality regressions, (3) rollout cadence (canary -> ramp -> full), and (4) a unified dashboard for stakeholders to inspect regressions by model, route, and customer tier. This ticket scopes the PM-level orchestration, success criteria, stakeholder cadence, and handoffs to Eng/Design/SRE for the Q1 cost-economics OKR.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical initiative dashboard accessible in Console with widget links to: experiment results, cost delta heatmap, and failing prompts (if any)
Three prioritized experiments scheduled with owners: adaptive-batching-v2, ttl-kv-eviction-policy, dynamic-quant-guardrail
Rollout runbook published with automated rollback thresholds and postmortem checklist
OKR metric definition finalized and instrumented: tokens_per_dollar (weekly), p95 latency (route-level), quality_regression_rate
Stakeholder cadence (weekly triage + biweekly demo) documented and invited participants confirmed

progress_updates: 2026-01-08 | Asha Menon: Created ticket and invited cross-functional stakeholders (Eng: Liam, Priya; SRE: Mateo; Design: Claire). Initial hypothesis list of 12 experiments captured in the initiative doc.

2026-01-20 | Liam Rodriguez: Telemetry schema PR submitted (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821). Schema includes tokens_per_dollar, tokens_served, model_cost_estimate, and route_tagging. Review feedback from infra team incorporated.

2026-02-01 | Priya Shah (PM): Prioritized top 3 experiments based on expected unit-econ delta and implementation risk. Chosen: adaptive-batching-v2 (high potential, medium risk), ttl-kv-eviction-policy (medium potential, low risk), dynamic-quant-guardrail (medium potential, high risk).

2026-02-12 | Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Canary for ttl-kv-eviction-policy ran for 72h against subset of customers (10%). Observed 9.2% token reduction for short-chat routes; no customer-facing errors. Latency p95 increased 18ms on avg — within SLA but flagged for follow-up optimization.

2026-02-18 | Claire Ng (Design): Dashboard mock validated in review; added quality regression panel and links to failing prompt sampler. UX changes requested: add model-version selector and time-shift comparison control.

2026-02-20 | Liam Rodriguez: Canary telemetry shows early signal of token-per-dollar improvement for adaptive-batching-v2 when combined with prefix cache; scheduling A/B test for 2026-02-25. Added rollback thresholds (quality_regression_rate > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency > +50ms for 30m window).
decisions: Prioritize end-to-end experiments (batching + cache) over standalone quantization experiments in Q1 to maximize short-term token savings
Adopt a conservative rollout policy: canary (10%) -> ramp (50%) -> full (100%) with automated rollback triggers and manual triage for ambiguous signals
Quality regression gating: any A/B test that increases failing prompt rate by >1.25x must be paused and reviewed by Research & Quality team
Instrument tokens_per_dollar as primary OKR metric with weekly aggregation and cohort breakouts by model and route
risks: Quality regressions from quantization experiments could be subtle and not surface in token-level signals — requires prompt-level sampling and human review
Telemetry gaps for multi-model routes may obscure true unit-econ impact; need robust route tagging and attribution
Potential cross-talk between batching and cache changes (order of ops) could result in inconsistent improvements across customer workloads
Operational overhead: SRE/Eng runbook automation required to keep canary ramp safe — underinvestment delays rollouts
